changelog: Insert a fallback ordering that, when comparing two candidate cuts, prefers the cut that keeps a short function word (determiner/pronoun/auxiliary/preposition) together with the immediately following head or required complement — to reduce single-word fragments and orphaned dependents identified in the primary finding.
findings: The prompt overvalues cutting immediately after short function words and underestimates the damage of detaching those words from the content that completes the phrase, producing single-word fragments or orphaned dependents that harm cohesion or create contradictions.

The prompt allows cuts inside multiword names, organizational titles and tight enumerations, failing to protect named entities and listed items that must be translated as contiguous units for clarity.

edits.now: - Fallback ordering: when comparing two candidate cuts on the source surface, if

diagnosis.why: The new fallback ordering that prefers keeping short function words attached to their following head made the model avoid single-word fragments, which raised H_set for short-latency pieces (positive means in ≤3/≤5/≤7/≤10 bins) but shifted cut choices in longer sentences (slight negative for ≤99 and several large degradations), e.g. moving cuts into or out of quoted complements and splitting enumerations.
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should preserve the fallback’s clear benefit for very short pieces while avoiding broad application that repositions top cuts in long sentences and thereby breaks enumerations or quoted complements.
